annotations.text:
The pilot page, rethought. Friends stays a tab of its own; this is only the account page.

What every direction fixes:

KEEP THIS PILOT becomes SET A PASSWORD. The old label named a consequence and hid the act; the new one is the act, and it pairs with CHANGE PASSWORD once claimed.

The info box is gone everywhere. It said the call sign a third time, the password sentence a second time, and a paragraph of lore over an empty gap. What it knew now rides the controls that need it: one status line under the name, one note under the password key, and the rest lives in the claim card, where it was already written.

The reroll moves behind a NEW NAME key. Today a press on your own call sign rerolls it on the spot, rate cap or not, which is a landmine on the row a curious player presses first.

A - PLAIN WORDS. The smallest change: same list grammar, honest labels, the box deleted, reroll behind its key.

For: shippable in an afternoon, and nothing new to learn.
Against: the page is three rows over an empty column; cleaner, but still a room with nothing in it.

B - PILOT CARD (leading). Identity leads: the name large, the status line under it, the one warning a guest needs, and the acts as keys. Under it, the career: the facts that make the page worth opening.

Every career field already exists. Rating, tier, games, kills and deaths are published per pilot at /pilots today, and rivets is already on the client; showing them here is one meta call. Guests have careers too, which is quietly the best claim pitch on the page: a record worth keeping is standing right above the key that keeps it.

For: the page finally answers a question (how am I doing) instead of only asking one; both complaints fixed as a side effect.
Against: needs that meta call; without it the career section must wait, and B collapses to A with a bigger head.

C - THE FORM IS THE PAGE. For a guest the page is the claim form itself: password field inline, one lit key, log in below as the alternative. No card opens over an empty page.

For: the emptiness becomes the form's room; the claim flow loses a step.
Against: a form pointed at every guest reads as a demand, and the house rule is that a password is offered, never demanded. Claimed, the form has nothing to ask and the page is back to being thin.
CURRENT, for scale. Three rows, then a box that repeats them with a paragraph of lore over 170 points of nothing. The name appears three times on one screen.
